items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And he used to idolize Dorothy Donegan because she was such a great performer.

ctx.x: Oh, sure, sure. I did many of those. Prior to getting into more jazz, I used to do quite a bit of what we call Rhythm & Blues and entertainment type group things. They were a lot of fun you know, and very beneficial to your growth also because you get a feeling of entertainment, which all music is, you know. And no matter how serious it is, it’s still supposed to be entertaining. I remember playing with a group, Johnny “Guitar” Saunders, he was a guitar player naturally, and he had a nice entertainment type…

and play the Pueblo Club. And I played with that group a lot for a while. Then I played with another wonderful trio, Eugene Smith. He was very entertaining. He would do a lot of piano, stand up and play the piano and sing and do stuff like that. You know like Maurice Rocco, but Maurice Rocco used to dance. He was a tremendous dancer. And he would dance and play the piano. “Boogie Woogie” and everything. Eugene is very good like that. And he used to idolize Dorothy Donegan because she was such a great performer.…
Tell me about playing on this particular recording with Milt.
